info.name: HipTen MuleSoft (yp-integration)
info.description:
HipTen's MuleSoft app between YourPolicy's Salesforce and Applied Epic.

USAGE:
1. Import this collection and the environments (Local, Dev, UAT).
2. Pick the environment top right. client_id / client_secret (API Manager client app 'Salesforce UAT') are filled in for Dev and UAT.
3. Run Health, then Connection Test, then the Files folder top to bottom.

Every call needs the client_id and client_secret headers (Client ID Enforcement in API Manager, instance 21216714).
Locally the policy is off, but the API spec still requires the two headers, so any value works.
Local uses a self-signed certificate: SSL verification is switched off on these requests.

exec: // Errors from the app carry a correlationId; quote it when checking the Mule logs.
let j = {}; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {}
if (pm.response.code === 401 && j.error) console.warn('401 from API Manager: check client_id / client_secret for this environment.');

request.description: App is up. Returns status, application, environment (mule.env) and timestamp.

Checks both legs:
- salesforce: reads the integration user's own User record (JWT bearer).
- appliedEpic: gets an Applied token (cached in the app) and calls GET /epic/client/v1/clients?limit=1.

Body fields are required by the API spec: source must be "Salesforce", orgId 15-18 chars, sentAt a datetime.

item.name: Files (Applied Epic attachments)
item.description:
Full local test of the files API. Run the folders in order (Run collection works too).

1 Supported files: list, then the same PDF previewed and downloaded; single-use download; the PDF through the Policy record.
2 Files that can't be previewed: Word, .eml, .msg refused for preview, downloaded fine.
3 Files Applied sends without a download link: the list can't tell, Get link answers NOT_AVAILABLE.
4 Access checks and bad requests.
5 List: policy, paging, unknown records, bad input.

Each OK Get link writes a Log__c row in the Salesforce dev org (no file name, PHI rule).
Everything should pass.

resultCode values: OK, NOT_FOUND, REFUSED, NOT_AVAILABLE, TOO_LARGE (off: no preview size limit yet), UNAVAILABLE.
Test data: Applied sandbox (S1). Only Local runs this code for now.

item.name: 3 Files Applied sends without a download link
item.description:
93% of 300 random files in the Applied sandbox come back with an empty download link (file.url), at any size. Applied still reports them as OK, so the list shows them as available and offers Preview on PDFs. We only find out at Get link: the answer must be NOT_AVAILABLE ("This file could not be opened. Try again"), with no link and no Log__c row.

The test client for this folder has 35 files and none of them has a link.

item.name: 3.1 List a client whose files have no link

request.description: Shows the problem: every file looks available and the PDFs say canPreview true, although none can be opened.

pm.test('PDFs say canPreview true', () => pm.expect(f.filter(x => x.type === 'pdf' && x.canPreview).length).to.be.above(0));
